label: sparse early-input-phase feature on idiosyncratic prefix combinations (e.g. m/o, 1/2, p, then h/p/e)
explanation: Very sparse (0.02% of steps). Fires almost only in the original-input phase at steps 2-5 (about 60% of mass at t=3, 29% at t=4). It never fires at t=0-1 or in the copy phase, and fires only twice on the delimiter. Within that window it responds to a conjunction of the current input and the first few tokens. Top examples have first token m or o (m is 41% of mass), the token two back is 1, 2 or p, the previous token is p, and the current input is h, p, e, g, z or a. Example: m 1 p [h], m p p [h], m 2 p [e]. The strongest activations (0.9-1.0 of max) are on the exact prefix m {1,2,p} p followed by one of those letters. Weaker ones are on looser near-matches (x p p y, 1 1 1 h, o 1 2 2). No single token condition is close to sufficient: m ? p at t=3 has precision 0.13. The best trigram conjunction reaches dev F1 0.22 (precision 0.16, recall 0.35, mass recall 0.37), and widening the sets raises recall only by losing a lot of precision. It looks like a hash-like detector for a set of specific early prefixes, with no compact explanation.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev2_tok=1 (+4.87), prev_tok=p (+4.48), orig0=m (+4.44), prev2_tok=p (+3.72), prev2_tok=2 (+3.33), prev_tok=1 (+3.33). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-3.87).
